key_insight: LLM agent skills are not isolated artifacts—they form dependency-bearing supply chains where hidden package, service, and recursive skill dependencies can create duplication, inconsistency, and security risk.
engineering_relevance: For agent infrastructure, this means skill systems need SBOM-like dependency tracking, version/provenance visibility, and risk-aware governance to manage installation and security at scale.
method: Introduced Agent Skill Supply Chains (ASSCs) to model mixed skill-package-service dependency graphs.
Built SkillDepAnalyzer to extract natural-language dependency evidence and recover skill metadata and graphs.
Analyzed over 1.43 million skills to uncover structural patterns and security signals in dependencies.
evidence_signal: On the SKILL-DEP benchmark, SkillDepAnalyzer recovered skill metadata and dependency graphs more accurately and comprehensively than an LLM-based baseline and package-centric SBOM tools.
watch_item: Dependency evidence extracted from natural language may miss implicit or undocumented relationships, so incomplete manifests and evolving skill contents remain an implementation risk.
paper_title: Skills Are Not Islands: Measuring Dependency and Risk in Agent Skill Supply Chains
